phd.title: Prakruti Māyé
phd.subtitle: Using Virtual Reality to Deconstruct Insect Ecology
phd.text: For my PhD, I built a three-dimensional virtual environment for flies, with visual scenery, wind and odour. We found that apple flies used perspective and motion parallax to distinguish objects of different sizes and distances. They also combined odour with directional airflow to follow a host plume.
phd.people: My advisor was Shannon B. Olsson, and Sanjay P. Sane was on my thesis committee. Marian Renz, whom I mentored as a BSc student, co-authored the PNAS paper with us.
phd.awards: During this work, I received a Microsoft Research grant in 2018, the Infosys Travel Award in 2019, and a full scholarship to the 2019 Janelia Mechanistic Cognitive Neuroscience Junior Scientist Workshop.
phd.press: The paper was covered by CNN, Haaretz, Phys.org and Der Tagesspiegel.
phd.summary: For my PhD, I built a virtual world for flies. We found that apple flies combined visual depth cues, wind and odour to find distant targets.

matrex.title: MATREX VR
matrex.text: I’m developing MATREX, a modular virtual-reality system for insect experiments. It combines visual scenery, odour and airflow, and can run off-grid. I use it with collaborators to study animals in the field as well as in the lab.
matrex.support: This work has received support from CASCB (2024) and a Smithsonian Tropical Research Institute small grant (2026).
matrex.talks: I’ve presented the field VR work at DZG (2023), SICB and ICN (2024), and Behavior 2025 in Kolkata.
